conviction_note: One large, mostly mechanical item: the 5-year Treasury rose about 90bp in Q3 (4.19% on 30 Jun to 5.09% on 30 Sep, Treasury par curve), and River City carries undesignated pay-fixed swaps whose mark-to-market runs through income. Its own releases show +$1.7m on +19bp (Q1-26), +$3.2m on +27bp (Q2-26) and -$6.4m on -42bp (Q1-25), so Q3 likely holds a pre-tax MTM gain of roughly $6-12m, about +$0.30-0.60 a share, against a $1.22-1.27 consensus that matches Q2's core EPS excluding MTM (~$1.21). GAAP EPS likely prints well above consensus (print_vs_bar about +30%). Management says outright that these MTM gains are not economic, KBW, Raymond James, Stephens and D.A. Davidson model the bank, and rates have already given back about a third of the Q3 move since quarter-end (5y 4.78% on 22 Oct). So the reaction is sized as a one-off: p_up 56 on abs_move 3.5 gives +0.42. That is close to the findings' sum of +0.6 by coincidence, not by fitting. The stock sits at the $56 average analyst target after a +8% 20-day run, which holds p_up near 50.

findings.finding: The Q3 GAAP print very likely includes a large swap mark-to-market gain. River City's undesignated interest-rate swaps (about 17% of its swap book at 30 Jun 2026) hedge medium-term fixed-rate loans and gain when rates rise. Its own releases record +$4.3m in Q1-24 on rising rates, -$6.4m in Q1-25 (5y -42bp), +$1.73m in Q1-26 (5y +19bp) and +$3.18m in Q2-26 (5y +27bp), about $0.09-0.15m per bp. The 5-year Treasury rose 90bp in Q3-26 (4.19% on 30 Jun to 5.09% on 30 Sep) and the 2-year rose 74bp. That implies a Q3 pre-tax MTM gain of about $6-12m, or +$0.30-0.60 a share on ~14.0m shares after ~30% tax. Consensus is about $1.26 (Q2 core excluding MTM ~ $1.21), so GAAP EPS could print around $1.55-1.85, and revenue around $45-50m against the $38-39m revenue consensus. Caveats folded into the size: management states it does not treat MTM as economic, the bank may have designated more swaps during Q3 (undesignated share went 15% to 17% in Q2), and the 5y had fallen back to 4.78% by 22 Oct, so a Q4-to-date reversal of roughly a third is visible to anyone who asks on the call.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No usable reaction history. RCBC listed on Nasdaq on 2026-08-06 and this is its first print as a listed company; earlier prints were OTC and the baseline has no EDGAR history (bank-level FDIC filer). The company itself has flagged MTM as non-economic since at least Q1-24, so holders who knew the name OTC are used to looking through it.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at $1.22-1.27 sits at or below Q2's GAAP $1.37 and at Q2's core excluding MTM, so the estimates carry no material MTM gain. The revenue consensus ($38-39m) is below Q2's $40.5m GAAP revenue, which included a $3.2m MTM gain. If the market had priced a GAAP blowout, the estimate range would sit near $1.6-1.8. The stock's +8% 20-day run may partly reflect rates-sensitive bank buying, but it carries no label. What stays unpriced is the headline 'beat' that screeners and aggregators will print. Whether holders pay for it is the open question, so the size is a fraction of the same dollars as core profit.

The sensitivity per bp is my inference from four company-reported quarters, not a company-stated DV01.

findings.finding: The Fed raised the funds target 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, the first hike in this cycle. River City's NIM fell from 2.59% (Q2-25) to 2.38% (Q1-26) to 2.34% (Q2-26) as policy rates were cut, and its pay-fixed/receive-floating swaps turn its fixed-rate loans floating. Read together, the bank looks asset-sensitive, so the hike is a likely tailwind for Q4 NII and NIM commentary on the 26 Oct call. Q3 itself only gets two weeks of the hike, and cost of deposits is high (2.77%), so a deposit-beta drag partly offsets.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: None: the bank gives no numeric guidance and this is its first listed call. No observed reaction to NIM commentary.
findings.why_not_priced: Analysts' FY27 EPS ($4.98) is flat on FY26 ($4.96) per stockanalysis, which does not look like a model with an NIM lift from a hike that was not expected when they initiated on 31 Aug. If priced, FY27 estimates would have been raised after 16 Sep. This is weak evidence because estimate revisions are not visible.
findings.independence: The NIM series comes from the company's Q2-26 release as tabulated by StockTitan (https://www.stocktitan.net/news/RCBC/river-city-bank-reports-net-income-of-19-6-million-for-the-second-ty3ieti73zwf.html). The asset-sensitivity reading is my inference; the company has not stated a rate-sensitivity number that I could reach. FY estimates: https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/rcbc/forecast/. This is a proxy: macro-to-company transmission not confirmed by the company.
